newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul stocks close lower on consolidation.
newsitem.headline: Seoul stocks close lower on consolidation.

text.p: Consolidation following last week's rises pushed Seoul stocks to close lower on Tuesday as worries about growing inter-Korean tension still lingered in the market, brokers said.
The composite stock index fell 5.99 points to 706.94, off a day low of 703.99. Losers led gainers by 536 to 258.
"The market appeared to lose its elasticity due to external factors such as the inter-Korean issue and the Hanbo loan scandal," said Kim Duck-sun of Hyundai Securities.
Casey Choe of Union Bank of Switzerland forecast the index would consolidate to the 680 level.
Brokers said blue chips would be in demand tomorrow on news that South Korea was considering the early expansion of the foreign stock holding limit to slow a sharp rise in the dollar against the won.
The limit is due to be raised to 23 percent some time this year, from the current 20 percent.

A finance ministry official said in a phone interview the government was mulling diverse measures, including raising the ceiling, to slow the won's fall against the dollar. "Blue chips will benefit from the news. But the impact will not last if there are no further details," Choe said.

South Korean Prime Minister on Tuesday called for "extraordinary alertness" against North Korea, saying the defection of Hwang Jang-yop, a top advisor to Pyongyang leader Kim Jong-il, showed serious instability in the impoverished North Korea.

Brokers said the market was closely watching developments from a parliamentary session which has launched a new probe into the Hanbo Steel scandal. Opposition parties planned to call Kim Hyun-chul, the second son of President Kim Young-sam, to a parliamentary hearing over the loan. But the younger Kim has denied the allegation of his connection with the loan.
Kim Hyun-chul filed a criminal libel complaint on Tuesday against six opposition politicians on defamation over the loan scandal. Prosecutors said they would question Kim and the six soon.

Profit-taking dragged LG Semicon and Hyundai Electronics down by 1,500 won and 2,600 won respectively to 23,000 and 30,000. Foreign buying on expections of a recovery in the memory chip business had earlier boosted the shares.
